title: The partner identity resolution operation, its claim set, its answer schema, the scope type PLACED and the lifetime of an answer are specified by no source
description: Four values an rwb-access slice of the partner identity resolution needs are absent from every source. (a) No operation exists for the resolution: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none is a partner identity operation, API Specification v4 declares no partner identity path with x-module P4, and Architecture v5 slide 14 names only /authorise, /me/permissions, /doa-limits and /masking-policies, so the path, the method and the access rule are fixed here from the base rule and carried as an assumption. (b) The claim set the external gateway supplies and the answer it receives have no schema in any source: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines partner_user with DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists only the RW- roles, so the claim names partnerIdentityRef, partnerId, partnerRoleCodes, firmPanelStatus, firmContractEnd, amr, route and tokenExpiry and the answer names roles, scope, matrixVersion, maskingVersion, expiry and decision are fixed here and each maps to a DF field or to a gateway claim. (c) The scope type PLACED is named by legacy RWB-E2-019 and by FSD P6 AC-P6-013-01 but is not a value of LOV-SCOPE in TSD P4 v3 T3.2, which holds OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, and no source says whether PLACED is a scope of the role model or a descriptor of a partner session; the answer carries it as a session descriptor and does not add it to the role default-scope list. The lifetime of an answer beyond the gateway token lifetime is also absent: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes a five-minute token lifetime for the partner edge and no source states how long a resolved answer may live, so the answer expires no later than the token. Nothing here blocks a build, because every value is a claim, a row, a parameter or a reference value read at run time and no literal appears in code.
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 14, 20, 29, 35 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1 and appendix T-A; API Specification v4 (no x-module P4 partner path); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 (REQ-ACA-012 and the role class only); FSD P6 Communications v3 AC-P6-013-01 (scope PLACED); legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 14; RWB-PLT-N007-INF section 11 (token lifetime); RWB-PLT-N007-INF 12.2 (the rwb-partner upstream)
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 12; section 7 AC6 and AC9; section 11 Data; section 12.1, 12.2 and 12.3; section 13 Components and Build steps 1 to 5; section 14 Validation and messages
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 reads API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no partner identity row; API Specification v4 carries x-module S9 on /partners and on the four /partner/instructions paths and no x-module P4 partner path; Architecture v5 slide 14 reads rwb-access IN as POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines partner_user (DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217) without a status, a contract end or a claim set; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE reads OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL with no PLACED value; FSD P6 v3 AC-P6-013-01 reads the session holds role PT-LAWFIRM, scope PLACED and partner LF-0012; RWB-PLT-N007-INF section 11 reads the access token lifetime as 5 minutes; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 12 defines a ScopeFilter with type PLACED, partnerId and instructionTypes and a PartnerStatus published interface, and names no operation, no claim and no answer schema.
area: rwb-access partner identity resolution: operation, claim set, answer schema and answer lifetime
owner_role: Solution architect, P4 rwb-access with the external gateway owner
proposed: At the RWB-P4-E2019-CON contract review, confirm the resolution path on the P4 base, the claim names and the answer field names with the external gateway owner and the rwb-partner owner, and register the operation in the API specification and in TSD P4 appendix T-A with its schema. State in TSD P4 v3 T3.2 whether PLACED is a session scope descriptor or a role default scope. State the lifetime of a resolved answer against the token lifetime of the partner edge. Nothing here blocks the build: this story reads every value at run time and writes the placeholder wherever a literal would appear.

title: The contract of the partner identity resolution names no path, no claim or answer field, no refusal-to-status mapping and no statement of its absent events in any source
description: Four contract values are absent from every source. (a) The operation path is named nowhere: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and API Specification v4 declares no x-module P4 partner path, so the document fixes POST /partner-identities/resolve on the base /api/recovery/access/v1 from the base rule and duplicates no path of rwb-partner. (b) The claim and answer field names have no source: the legacy story publishes a Java interface with ScopeFilter and PartnerStatus and no wire shape, so the fields are fixed here and each is mapped to DF-REF-035, DF-REF-037, DF-REF-043, DF-REF-044, DF-REF-202, DF-REF-213 to DF-REF-215, DF-PRT-005 and DF-PRT-006 or to a gateway claim. (c) The mapping of a refusal to an HTTP status is not stated: the legacy story gives MSG-P4-001 on four different conditions, MSG-P4-005 without a reason code, MSG-P4-006 with an incident and MSG-P4-008 without a status, so the document fixes 400 for a malformed claim set, 401 for MSG-P4-001 and MSG-P4-005, 403 for MSG-P4-006 and MSG-P4-008 and 503 for MSG-P7-003. The absence of a published or consumed event is also unstated: Architecture v5 slide 14 calls rwb-access a reference-data owner with no event on the input side and names AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged as its only events, and no source says that a resolution publishes nothing, so the document states the absence and names the record as the DP-03 library event. Nothing here blocks the build, because the baseline is a document and its fakes.
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 41 and 42; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T5.3, T6.1 and appendix T-A; API Specification v4; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and AC-EXC-P4-001-03; legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 5, 7, 12 and 14
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 1 to 11; section 7 AC1 to AC6; section 11 Data; section 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4 and 12.7; section 13 Build steps 1 to 8; section 14 Validation and messages
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 has no partner identity operation and T-A.2 defines no partner schema; API Specification v4 declares x-module S9 on /partners and on the four /partner/instructions paths; Architecture v5 slide 14 reads rwb-access EVT as (none: reference data owner) and its OUT events as AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged only, and slide 11 fixes one RFC 9457 problem detail per error; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 names the conflict refusal with MSG-P4-006 and no status; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 5 gives MSG-P4-001 for no binding and for a bank identity on the partner route, MSG-P4-005 for no second factor without a status, MSG-P4-008 for a firm that has exited without a status, and MSG-P4-003 with status 404 for an instruction of another firm; section 12 publishes Java interfaces only.
area: rwb-access contract baseline of the partner identity resolution
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-access with the external gateway owner and the rwb-partner service owner
proposed: At the contract review, register the resolution operation and its two schemas in the API specification and in TSD P4 appendix T-A, agree the refusal-to-status table with the gateway owner and the message catalogue, and state in the document that the capability publishes no event and consumes none. Nothing here blocks the build: the baseline is a document with fakes, and the review freezes the names before the resolver and the DMZ slice depend on them.

title: The certificate profile, the rotation and revocation of the rwb-access hop, the numeric rate limit and the namespace and service names of the DMZ hop are specified by no source
description: Four infrastructure values of the hop from the partner gateway to rwb-access are absent from every source. (a) The certificate profile of the hop, its lifetime, its rotation window and the revocation propagation are named for the partner client at the gateway by RWB-PLT-N007-INF and are not stated for the gateway-to-rwb-access hop, so this story applies one profile to both ends and fixes the rotation inside an overlap window with a suspension at the deadline. (b) The per-client rate limit, its burst, its window and its retry hint on the resolution route are stated by no source: RWB-PLT-N007-INF fixes per-client limits for the partner portal route and NFR-003 sizes the partner population, so this story adopts the platform limit of the gateway and states the values it tests against. (c) The namespace, the service name and the port of rwb-access are not fixed by any source read: Architecture v5 slide 29 fixes the schema and the login and names no Kubernetes service, so the story writes namespace rwb-recovery and the rwb-access service port as the deployment defines them and names no number. The egress and ingress policy shape is also absent: no source states a NetworkPolicy object, so the story fixes one namespace, one service and one port in both directions, deny by default. Nothing here blocks a build, because every value is configuration applied by the infrastructure team and the platform defaults are recorded as the values the tests use.

section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 5 Exception paths X1 to X9; section 7 AC2 to AC5; section 11 Data; section 12.2 and 12.9; section 13 Build steps 1 to 8; section 14 Validation and messages
evidence: RWB-PLT-N007-INF section 11 reads the certificate as valid for 12 months and the revocation as effective within 30 days at the latest, for the partner client; its section 12.2 names rwb-partner as the only upstream and no rwb-access hop; Architecture v5 slide 29 reads one login per service in one ACE database and names no Kubernetes service or port; slide 35 reads every call encrypted and identified both ways with no lifetime; NFR-003 reads about 50 partner users online in the busiest hour of about 320 named users; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 19 leaves the architecture change of the external access out of scope and names no certificate, no policy and no limit.
area: DMZ hop from the partner gateway to rwb-access: certificate, policy and rate limit
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure with the security design authority
proposed: At the security design authority review of RWB-PLT-N007-INF, extend the certificate profile and the rotation window to the rwb-access hop, record the per-client limit and its burst for the resolution route in the gateway configuration baseline, and publish the namespace, service and port of rwb-access with the platform deployment so the NetworkPolicy names them from a source. Nothing here blocks the build: every value is configuration and the recorded defaults are the values the tests use.
